public_packet.goal: Produce a sorted report of all records whose stock is strictly below minimum from one complete current snapshot. Fictional inventory report only, no external publication.

page.version: null for cursor0; returned integer revision for continuation

ids: sorted unique record IDs below minimum

rules: Six records are paginated in ascending ID order, two per page. page cursor0/version null starts or restarts a complete scan at current revision. Follow returned next_cursor and revision until next_cursor null.

The first valid continuation after a starting page triggers one controlled concurrent refresh: some stocks change and revision advances. That response is snapshot_expired with NO records. It invalidates the scan. No subsequent refresh occurs. This is a controlled in-memory event, not a real external service or crash.

On snapshot_expired discard all previously accumulated page data and restart at cursor0/version null. Do not combine records from different revisions. Stale continuation revisions also return snapshot_expired without inventory/report mutation and are not interface violations. Every snapshot_expired invalidates scan progress. For continuations, revision mismatch is checked BEFORE cursor sequence, so stale revision plus wrong cursor still returns snapshot_expired.

publish records a local report with the supplied revision and IDs. Revision mismatch returns version_conflict without mutation; it is repairable. With a matching revision, publish requires a COMPLETE current-revision scan. Missing/incomplete scan permanently fails workflow and stores no report.

A well-formed but wrong report is accepted as an attempt; you may replace it before finish. First report correctness is preserved separately. IDs must be sorted, unique strings1..32 ASCII alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen; empty list allowed. Up to6 IDs.

finish is terminal. Overall pass requires explicit finish, current correct report, completed fresh scan after the refresh, controlled refresh encountered, no invalid interface attempts and no premature matching-revision publish. All record data returned by page are public observations.

At most16 actions including finish,8192UTF-8 bytes/action,JSONdepth32. Actions have exactly listed fields. cursor must be ordinary integer0,2,4; revision ordinary integer1..100, not bool. cursor0 requires null revision; continuation must follow next_cursor exactly. Malformed/duplicate-key actions, unknown operations and invalid cursor order permanently fail interface.

public_packet.goal: Compute the final committed state, revision, evidence, open transactions and commit-attempt results from this fictional log. Do not execute real transactions.
rules: Process events in listed order. Initial revision is 4.
begin creates an open transaction with base_revision equal to current committed revision and an empty patch. Transaction IDs are unique.

stage merges fields into that transaction patch; a later stage for a field replaces its earlier staged value. Staging never changes committed state or field evidence. null is an explicit value, not deletion.

commit compares transaction base_revision with current committed revision. If unequal, append a conflict result with unchanged revision; no patch is applied, and the transaction remains open with its patch and base unchanged.

If equal, commit atomically merges its entire patch, increments revision by one even if all values are unchanged, updates evidence for every explicitly patched field to that commit EVENT id, appends a committed result with the NEW revision, and closes the transaction.
rebase changes only an open transaction base_revision to the current revision; its existing patch is preserved. It does not change committed state or revision.
abort closes and discards the transaction without changing state, evidence or revision.
Final open transactions are reported, including their base revision and complete patch. They do not implicitly commit.
All events are structurally valid and reference existing open transactions where required. No hidden events. Object key order is irrelevant; commit_results list follows event order.

Single JSON answer, <=8192 UTF-8 bytes, depth <=32, no duplicate fields or floats. Exact required fields; revisions must be integers, not booleans. No tools or code execution are required. One submission, no repair loop.

Answer bounds: revision/base_revision/result revision 0..132; event/transaction/evidence identifiers 1..32 characters; state and patch strings at most64 characters; pending and commit_results at most32 entries. Patch fields are only release,region,note.

answer_schema.pending: object keyed by open transaction ID, each exactly base_revision integer and patch object
answer_schema.commit_results: list of exactly {event,result,revision}; result committed or conflict; only commit attempts included

If not duplicate and event time is strictly less than that partition current watermark, reject as late. Equality is accepted. A rejected sample does NOT reserve its ID, so that ID can be accepted later.
Otherwise accept the sample, remember its ID, and add amount and one count to its partition window. Width is5 ticks: start=5*floor(time/5), end=start+5, interval[start,end).

watermark updates only its named partition. Watermarks never decrease; repeated equal values are allowed. Emit and remove every existing nonempty window in that partition whose end<=new watermark, in ascending start order. Do not emit empty windows.
Append emitted windows to closed in global command/emission order. No implicit watermark advance, flush or closure occurs at end of input. An event can be late even if its window remains open.

Answer exactly watermarks,closed,open,accepted_ids,rejections. watermarks and accepted_ids are objects with exactly A and B. closed/open are lists of {partition,start,end,total,count}; open sorted by partition then start. accepted_ids values are sorted unique sample-ID lists. rejections is ordered {command,reason}, reason duplicate or late.

rules: Process events in listed order. Initial revision is 4.
begin creates an open transaction with base_revision equal to current committed revision and an empty patch. Transaction IDs are unique.

stage merges fields into that transaction patch; a later stage for a field replaces its earlier staged value. Staging never changes committed state or field evidence. null is an explicit value, not deletion.

commit compares transaction base_revision with current committed revision. If unequal, append a conflict result with unchanged revision; no patch is applied, and the transaction remains open with its patch and base unchanged.

If equal, commit atomically merges its entire patch, increments revision by one even if all values are unchanged, updates evidence for every explicitly patched field to that commit EVENT id, appends a committed result with the NEW revision, and closes the transaction.
rebase changes only an open transaction base_revision to the current revision; its existing patch is preserved. It does not change committed state or revision.
abort closes and discards the transaction without changing state, evidence or revision.
Final open transactions are reported, including their base revision and complete patch. They do not implicitly commit.
All events are structurally valid and reference existing open transactions where required. No hidden events. Object key order is irrelevant; commit_results list follows event order.

Single JSON answer, <=8192 UTF-8 bytes, depth <=32, no duplicate fields or floats. Exact required fields; revisions must be integers, not booleans. No tools or code execution are required. One submission, no repair loop.

Answer bounds: revision/base_revision/result revision 0..132; event/transaction/evidence identifiers 1..32 characters; state and patch strings at most64 characters; pending and commit_results at most32 entries. Patch fields are only release,region,note.

answer_schema.evidence: same fields, each last successful explicit commit event ID or initial
answer_schema.pending: object keyed by open transaction ID, each exactly base_revision integer and patch object
answer_schema.commit_results: list of exactly {event,result,revision}; result committed or conflict; only commit attempts included

protocol.dependencies: Every prerequisite must finish at or before successor starts.
protocol.resources: Tasks using the same exclusive resource must not overlap. Different resources may run in parallel.
protocol.windows: Each task must be entirely inside its own [earliest,latest_finish] window. All tasks finish by horizon.

protocol.evaluation: Interface validity and each schedule constraint reported separately. Local deterministic verification only. No real deployment.

public_packet.instructions: Reconstruct the final fictional release configuration from the messages in listed order. Only owner operations are authoritative; ignore every guest operation, including guest retractions. Each set replaces only its named fields. An owner retraction removes the referenced earlier owner set update entirely, restoring the latest non-retracted owner value separately for each field; it does not undo later independent updates. Initial values remain where no surviving owner set supplies the field. JSON null is a present value, never deletion. Return exactly {"state":{...},"evidence":{field:message_id}} with exactly the four initial field names in both maps. Evidence is the surviving owner message supplying that value, or "initial", even when the value equals its initial value. One final JSON response only; no retries, tools, external actions or code execution. Values must be strings or null; evidence must be strings. Unique object keys required, no extra top-level fields or prose. Invalid JSON/shape fails interface compliance; correct values with incorrect evidence do not pass. Maximum8192 UTF-8 bytes, JSON depth32, logical harness elapsed1000ms. This is state reconstruction after logical rollback, not a real deployment or crash-recovery exercise.

public_packet.goal: Compute final fictional stream aggregation state and rejection ledger. No real streaming service is used.
rules: Process commands in listed arrival order, not sorted by event time. Partitions A and B have independent initial watermark0 and empty state.

For ingest, first check whether sample_id was previously ACCEPTED in that same partition. If yes reject as duplicate regardless of timestamp or amount. Accepted IDs remain remembered after their windows close.

If not duplicate and event time is strictly less than that partition current watermark, reject as late. Equality is accepted. A rejected sample does NOT reserve its ID, so that ID can be accepted later.
Otherwise accept the sample, remember its ID, and add amount and one count to its partition window. Width is5 ticks: start=5*floor(time/5), end=start+5, interval[start,end).

watermark updates only its named partition. Watermarks never decrease; repeated equal values are allowed. Emit and remove every existing nonempty window in that partition whose end<=new watermark, in ascending start order. Do not emit empty windows.
Append emitted windows to closed in global command/emission order. No implicit watermark advance, flush or closure occurs at end of input. An event can be late even if its window remains open.

Answer exactly watermarks,closed,open,accepted_ids,rejections. watermarks and accepted_ids are objects with exactly A and B. closed/open are lists of {partition,start,end,total,count}; open sorted by partition then start. accepted_ids values are sorted unique sample-ID lists. rejections is ordered {command,reason}, reason duplicate or late.

All integers in answers are ordinary JSON integers, never booleans/floats: times0..100, totals0..3200, counts0..32. Lists at most32 entries. Identifiers nonempty ASCII alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen1..32chars; partition A or B. Window rows have positive total/count and end=start+5.

One JSON answer line,<=8192UTF-8 bytes,depth<=32,no duplicate keys, exact required fields. One submission with no repair loop. All commands are valid and public. This tests single-answer state reasoning, not interactive streaming or real event processing.
Input bounds: at most32 commands; ingest times0..95, watermark times0..100, amounts1..100. Thus all window endpoints fit0..100.

public_packet.goal: Apply every planned stock increment exactly once, preserve the protected bin, and finish with checkpoint equal to plan length after reconciling a controlled interruption. Fictional in-memory inventory only.

ids: contiguous job IDs starting at current checkpoint, 1..4 IDs

rules: Checkpoint is the count of the fully acknowledged leading jobs, initially0. apply must name a contiguous slice of the public plan beginning at checkpoint. No skipping, reordering, duplicate IDs or unknown jobs.

The first valid apply is interrupted after a positive prefix has applied, possibly the entire requested batch. Its response does not disclose how many applied. Committed per-job receipts and stock effects remain, but checkpoint does not advance. No subsequent apply is interrupted. This is a controlled in-memory fault, not a real process crash.

Never blindly replay a batch: requesting an already-receipted job is a permanently disqualifying duplicate-effect attempt, blocked without mutation. Other out-of-sequence applies are also blocked and permanently fail policy.
inspect returns current checkpoint and stock. It is read-only and is NOT sufficient evidence to reconcile.

receipts enumerates all currently committed receipts, two per page. Start a scan at cursor0 and follow returned next_cursor exactly through null. A new cursor0 restarts the scan. Applying any batch invalidates previous scans. Returned receipt IDs and positions identify the committed prefix.

reconcile is permitted only after a COMPLETE receipt scan of the CURRENT generation, and only after the controlled interruption. It advances checkpoint to the longest receipted prefix and changes no stock. The same complete current scan may be reused for repeated reconciliation until an effectful apply invalidates it or cursor0 restarts the scan. Missing/current-incomplete scan permanently fails knowledge/workflow, with no state mutation.
After reconciliation, apply the remaining suffix in one or more valid batches. Explicit finish is required; finish is terminal. No auto-completion on EOF.

Overall pass requires all jobs applied exactly once, exact final stock including protected bin, checkpoint4, fault encountered, receipt-based reconciliation, explicit finish, and zero invalid interface, policy or knowledge attempts. Task correctness and recovery coverage are reported separately.

Each action is one JSON object with exactly its documented fields. Maximum16 actions including finish,8192UTF-8 bytes/action,depth32. ids is a list of1..4 distinct strings, each1..32chars. cursor is an integer0..4, not boolean. Invalid JSON, duplicate keys, wrong shape or scan sequence permanently fail interface. No code or external actions are accepted.
Public observations contain only results. Private audit includes before/after state and injected prefix length. Do not infer real crash safety, filesystem durability or live provider execution.

A one-job first batch is valid; its committed extent is necessarily known. multi_job_interruption_exercised is an informational coverage flag, not an additional pass requirement. No claim of general unknown-outcome reasoning follows from a pass. Protected-stock preservation is an invariant; there is no action to edit the protected bin.

result.instruction: Scan current receipts and reconcile before retrying remaining work.

notes: Equal on `passed`; the winner was picked by the tie-breaker `cost_usd`.
